parsed.study_design: Unbalanced utility-level panel study using pooled OLS and fixed- and random-effects regressions
parsed.population_and_sample: Urban and peri-urban populations within the service areas of 75 water utilities; the principal adjusted models used 225 utility-year observations from 72 utilities in 22 countries, with data spanning 1996–2009 and coverage outcomes measured through 2012.
parsed.exposure: Utility O&M cost-recovery ratio (collected operating revenues divided by operating and maintenance costs), including its squared term; models also examine public water expenditure, ODA, non-revenue water, urbanization, and regional controls.
parsed.outcome: Three-year absolute change in water-service coverage, defined as the percentage of the population under a utility's nominal responsibility with a direct connection or within reach of a public water point.
parsed.rationale: Section 3 (pp. 29–31) identifies the population, utility-level exposure, access outcome, data sources, sampling frame, and panel structure. Section 4 (pp. 31–33) reports empirical pooled OLS and fixed- and random-effects models showing a nonlinear association between cost recovery and subsequent coverage change. The conclusion (pp. 33–34) interprets this as a governance and regulatory trade-off: moderate cost recovery supports access expansion, whereas high targets may discourage service extension to poor and peri-urban populations.
